title: Faith, hope, love at work (1 Thessalonians 1)
hookLine: Paul remembers their work of faith, labor of love, patience of hope
tomorrow: give thanks in everything? even on the worst day of the week?

cards: Old work gloves tell on their owner. A hole worn through at the thumb, a stiff patch from a paint can, a palm gone smooth from years on the same handle. So do a coach's whistle, a nurse's shoes, a baker's burned knuckles.
Nobody needs a speech about what those hands did. A letter to the church in Thessalonica opens the same way. Paul, with Silvanus and Timothy, doesn't start by correcting anyone.
He gives thanks, and starts with what he remembers seeing them do.

teach.b: Here's the line: "Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love, and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ." Three pairs, and each ties a big word to something you could see.
Love shows up as labor, the effort that leaves a person tired.
Hope shows up as patience, staying put under pressure. Faith, hope and love: the same three Paul names together in First Corinthians thirteen. Here they've got their sleeves rolled up.
And it costs something. They "received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Ghost." Trouble and joy in one sentence.
And look at the direction it took. Paul says they "turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God." Turned, and then served: faith with somewhere to go and something to do.
Then a sound picture: "For from you sounded out the word of the Lord."
Other towns were already telling Paul about them, so much that he says he doesn't need to say a thing. In this letter faith isn't only a private opinion.
It's a reputation other people can describe, the way a pair of gloves can.

how: Some Christians use 1 Thessalonians 1:2–3 as a pattern for prayer: giving thanks for particular people and naming what they have seen them do.

games.q: at a funeral, the speaker says little about what the woman believed, only what she did for years: meals, rides, visits. a guest calls it a faithless eulogy. how would 1 Thessalonians 1 hear it?
o: as faith described: a work of faith, a labor of love, a patience of hope.
as a gap: faith should be stated in words, not shown in deeds.
as love only, since faith and hope can't be seen by anyone.
games.why: Paul's opening remembers what he saw them do. their faith sounded out, and other towns told the story for him.

practice: Turn your hands palm up in your lap and look at them: the lines, a scar, a callus, whatever is there.
Let one person come to mind whose hands you've watched do faithful work, and name one thing they did that was work, one that was labor, and one that was patience.
No need to say anything aloud; give each one a slow breath, and keep your hands open the whole time.

wordCard.voice: Faith. In First Thessalonians one, not only something held inside, but something you can see: a work of faith, beside love's labor and hope's patience, loud enough that other towns heard about it.

orig.note: Greek: faith, trust. In 1 Thessalonians 1:3 it's paired with work: the work of faith.

carryVoice: Your line: work, labor, patience. Faith, love and hope, each with its sleeves rolled up. That's today.
